local.h: Philadelphia details, checked against the City and the courts
bullets: Your ticket goes to the Traffic Division of the Philadelphia Municipal Court. The city's own page is blunt about the deadline: you must plead guilty or not guilty within 10 days of getting the ticket.
The Traffic Division does not handle parking, red-light or speed-camera tickets. Those belong to the Philadelphia Parking Authority, so do not try to pay a parking ticket through the court.
Pay, plead and ask for a hearing from the city's official page. Be careful with bookmarked links: Philadelphia changed payment vendors in January 2025, and the older portal no longer takes payments.
This is not an online-contest court. If you want to fight the ticket, plan on appearing.

At 6 points PennDOT requires you to attend its Driver Improvement School, and completing it removes 2 points. Three points also come off automatically for every 12 months you drive without a new violation.
Parking escalates fast: unpaid Philadelphia Parking Authority tickets lead to booting and towing, and you have to settle the balance in person to get the vehicle back.

cities.pay_label: Pennsylvania UJS portal (PAePay) - pay a citation by number
cities.court_label: Allegheny County courts - find your district court
cities.fine_note: Fines and court costs vary by violation. Check the court's current fine schedule, and treat the amount printed on your court notice as the real number.
cities.school_eligible: Pennsylvania has no voluntary course that erases a ticket on your own initiative. The record-saving conversations happen at the Magisterial District Court printed on your citation (or, in Philadelphia, the Municipal Court Traffic Division): ask about a plea to a lesser charge that carries no points, and about PennDOT's Driver Improvement School, which you must attend at 6 points and which removes 2 points on completion.
cities.points_note: Paying a Pennsylvania ticket counts as a guilty plea, so the points go on your PennDOT record. PennDOT takes action at 6 points and can suspend your licence at 11, and 3 points come off for every 12 months you drive without a new violation.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: On a Pennsylvania citation, box 1 is the Magisterial District Court number and box 2 is its address. That court - not the city - is where you pay, plead or ask for a hearing.

local.h: Pittsburgh details, checked against the Pennsylvania courts
bullets: Pittsburgh traffic citations are filed in the Magisterial District Court printed on the ticket - box 1 on a Pennsylvania citation is the district court number, box 2 is its address. That is where you pay, plead, or request a hearing.
Nearly everything can be done on the Pennsylvania UJS portal (ujsportal.pacourts.us), which is where PAePay lives. Search by citation number, docket number or payment-plan number.
Read the portal result carefully: not every case is payable online, and certain violations require an appearance. If the portal will not let you pay, that is the reason - it is not a broken website.
Parking tickets are not court cases. They come from the Pittsburgh Parking Authority, and you pay or contest those through the authority that issued the ticket.
Points run through PennDOT, not the county: action starts at 6 points, suspension can follow at 11, and 3 points come off for every 12 months without a new violation.

cities.pay_label: Franklin County Municipal Court Clerk - payment options
cities.court_label: Franklin County Municipal Court - Traffic Violations Bureau
cities.fine_note: Franklin County publishes the amount due on the case record. Look the case up first - the court only shows an online payment button when the case is marked payable.
cities.school_eligible: Ohio's record tool is a 2-point credit for completing a BMV-approved remedial driving course. It is a credit against your point total, and it does not delete a ticket unless a court orders it, so confirm what your court and the BMV will accept before you pay for a course.
cities.points_note: Ohio assesses points on conviction, and 12 points in two years triggers a 12-point suspension (a class-D suspension that typically runs six months). The BMV can act well before that, and points stay on your record for two years from the conviction.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Columbus tickets go to the Franklin County Municipal Court, and payable tickets are stored by the Traffic Violations Bureau for 30 days after the court date. If your case is not marked payable, you cannot fix it online - you have to deal with the court.
verify: whether your case is marked payable online
the exact fine and court costs for your violation
the current walk-in payment hours

local.h: Columbus details, checked against the Franklin County Clerk
bullets: Columbus citations go to the Franklin County Municipal Court. The Traffic Violations Bureau is on the first floor of the court building at 375 South High Street, and it manages tickets from Columbus Police, the Ohio State Highway Patrol, the Sheriff and the campus police.

Online: search the case first on the Clerk's records search. If the case is marked payable, a MAKE ONLINE PAYMENT button appears at the top. If it is not payable, online payment is simply not available for that case.

By mail: a money order or check payable to Franklin County Municipal Court. The court states plainly that no cash and no credit card are accepted by mail, and you must send a copy of your insurance card (not the original) if the proof-of-insurance box on the ticket is unchecked.
In person: the second floor is open from 7:30 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. every day to take payments.
Payable traffic minor misdemeanour tickets are held by the Bureau for 30 days after the court date. Miss that window and the case moves on without you.
Clerk's office for questions: (614) 645-8186. Bring your proof of insurance when you pay.

cities.pay_label: Cleveland Municipal Court - how to pay a traffic ticket

cities.school_eligible: Ohio's record tool is a 2-point credit for completing a BMV-approved remedial driving course. It is a credit against your point total, and it does not delete a ticket unless a court orders it, so confirm what your court and the BMV will accept before you pay for a course.
cities.points_note: Ohio assesses points on conviction, and 12 points in two years triggers a 12-point suspension (a class-D suspension that typically runs six months). The BMV can act well before that, and points stay on your record for two years from the conviction.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Cleveland splits traffic from parking. Moving violations go to the Municipal Court; parking citations go to the Clerk's Parking Violations Bureau on a different website and phone line.

local.h: Cleveland details, checked against the Clerk of Courts
bullets: Cleveland moving violations are handled by the Cleveland Municipal Court and its Waiver Bureau. The Clerk of Courts sits at 1200 Ontario Street, Cleveland, Ohio 44113.

Online: the Clerk's page links straight to the payment system - click through from the court's own site rather than searching, because third-party 'pay your ticket' sites charge extra and are not the court.
By mail: send a check or money order to Cleveland Municipal Court / Waiver Bureau / P.O. Box 99639 / Cleveland, Ohio 44199-0639.
In person: some offences require a court appearance. If you cannot complete the payment online, the court says to call 216-664-4790 or email clerkofcourts@cmcoh.org.
Parking is separate. Cleveland parking citations go through the Parking Violations Bureau (216-664-4744), which has its own payment site and its own contest process.
Ohio points land on your BMV record, and 12 points in two years triggers a 12-point suspension - typically six months. A BMV-approved remedial course earns a 2-point credit.

cities.pay_label: 36th District Court - payment methods
cities.court_label: 36th District Court, Detroit - court home page
cities.fine_note: Fines and court costs vary by violation. Check the court's current fine schedule, and treat the amount printed on your court notice as the real number.
cities.school_eligible: Michigan's real record saver is the Basic Driver Improvement Course (BDIC), run by the Secretary of State: an eligible driver who completes it avoids the points, and the ticket is not reported to insurance. You may only use it once, the State mails you a notice with a 60-day deadline to enrol, and you are not eligible if you already had more than 2 points when the ticket was issued, if the offence was criminal, if it happened in a commercial vehicle, if the ticket was issued outside Michigan, or if you hold a CDL.
cities.points_note: Michigan assesses points on conviction and keeps them for two years from the conviction date. 12 points in two years triggers a Secretary of State driver reexamination, which can end in a restriction, a suspension or a revocation.
cities.lawyer_cost: $300-$600 typical for a Detroit traffic citation
cities.tool_note: Michigan mails you the chance to avoid the points: if your ticket qualifies, the Secretary of State sends a letter and you have 60 days to enrol in the Basic Driver Improvement Course. Miss the letter and the points and the violation go to your insurer.
verify: whether your citation qualifies for the Basic Driver Improvement Course
the current fine, costs and late fees
whether your offence requires an appearance

local.h: Detroit details, checked against the 36th District Court
bullets: Detroit traffic cases go to the 36th District Court at 421 Madison Street, Detroit, MI 48226 - one of the busiest courts in the country.
Online: the court runs its own online payment form. By phone: payments are taken 24 hours a day, in English or Spanish, on 1-855-798-1547.
Kiosks: the court operates payment kiosks across Metro Detroit, plus one right outside the building on Brush Street. Cashier's window: 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday.
By mail or drop box: put the citation number on a check or money order payable to 36th District Court. Never mail or deposit cash.
Cannot pay in full? The court runs an Online Collections Application for monthly payment plans over traffic tickets.

The record saver in Michigan is the Basic Driver Improvement Course (BDIC). Complete it and the ticket is not reported to your insurer, but you can only use it once, you must act inside the State's 60-day deadline, and you are out of luck if you already had more than 2 points, the offence was criminal, it happened in a commercial vehicle, the ticket came from outside Michigan, or you hold a CDL.

cities.pay_label: Davidson County - pay a traffic ticket online
cities.court_label: Davidson County Circuit Court Clerk - Traffic Violation Bureau
cities.fine_note: Fines and court costs vary by violation. Check the court's current fine schedule, and treat the amount printed on your court notice as the real number.
cities.school_eligible: Tennessee does let a course help, in two different ways. A court-ordered traffic school can get a citation dismissed if the judge allows it, and separately the Department of Safety will remove up to 5 points from a speeding conviction if you complete an approved 4-hour driver education course. Course providers must send your certificate to the Department within 30 days, so ask the school who files it.
cities.points_note: Tennessee's Department of Safety runs a driver-improvement point system: 12 points in 12 months can bring a proposed suspension and a hearing. Points stay on your record for years, and it is the insurance effect that usually costs the most.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Davidson County's own office warns about ticket scams, so check the address bar: the only official payment site is the Clerk's paytraffic.nashville.gov, and the Traffic Violation Bureau is inside the county courthouse.
verify: the exact amount owed and the deadline printed on your citation
whether your violation is a payable one
which traffic schools your court will accept

local.h: Nashville details, checked against the Clerk's own site
bullets: Nashville and Davidson County citations are handled by the Traffic Violation Bureau, part of the Davidson County Circuit Court Clerk's Office, at 408 2nd Avenue North, Suite 1160.
Pay online through paytraffic.nashville.gov - that is the Clerk's own payment site.

The Clerk's office publishes a public alert about outstanding-ticket scams. Genuine court business will not arrive as a text demanding immediate payment; if you get one, call the Bureau instead of clicking.
Court dockets for traffic and Metro citations are published by the Bureau, so you can check your own court date and outcome without going through a paid lookup service.
The Bureau also handles installment payment requests with a motion form - useful if the fine will not fit in one month.

Tennessee will remove up to 5 points from a speeding conviction if you complete an approved 4-hour driver education course, and a court-ordered traffic school can get the citation dismissed outright if the judge agrees. Course providers must file your certificate within 30 days.

cities.pay_label: Mecklenburg County payment information (NC Judicial Branch)
cities.court_label: NC eCourts Portal - look up and pay a citation
cities.fine_note: North Carolina fines plus court costs, and the costs are often larger than the fine. The court's own notice is the amount that counts.
cities.school_eligible: North Carolina does not use traffic school. The three standard moves are a plea to a lesser speed (generally 9 mph over or less, which avoids insurance points), a plea to Improper Equipment, and a Prayer for Judgment Continued (a PJC, where the court withholds judgment so no points post). The limits and the insurance treatment differ, so confirm what your court will accept.
cities.points_note: North Carolina runs two point systems at once, and the insurance one costs far more. Convictions add DMV points (12 points in three years can suspend your licence), while insurers use a separate scale where a single insurance point commonly raises premiums by around 30%.
cities.lawyer_cost: $200-$400 typical for a Charlotte speeding ticket
cities.tool_note: North Carolina is the one state where the insurance system punishes harder than the licence system. One insurance point is commonly a 30% premium increase, which is why a plea to 9 mph over or to Improper Equipment is worth asking about.
verify: whether your citation is payable by mail or online
the current DMV and insurance point treatment for your exact speed
how many Prayers for Judgment Continued your court will allow

local.h: Charlotte details, checked against the NC Judicial Branch
bullets: Mecklenburg County citations are processed by the Clerk of Superior Court at the Mecklenburg County Courthouse. The mailing address for payments is PO Box 37971, Charlotte, NC 28237-7971.

By mail the Clerk takes a money order or certified check only - no cash and no personal cheques - payable to Mecklenburg County Clerk of Superior Court, and you should include a copy of the citation. Only pay by mail if your citation is marked as eligible.
In person at the Cashier's Office you can use cash, card, money order or certified check; card payments add a processing fee, and there is an ATM on Level 2.
Online, North Carolina moved to the statewide eCourts Portal. That is where you find the case, see whether it is payable, and pay it if it is.

The interesting move in North Carolina is not a course, it is the plea: 9 mph over or less avoids insurance points, Improper Equipment avoids them too, and a PJC (Prayer for Judgment Continued) has the court withhold judgment. Ask the clerk or a local attorney what your court will accept, because the limits are enforced.
DMV points and insurance points are different scales. 12 DMV points in three years can suspend your licence; a single insurance point can raise your premium by roughly 30%.

cities.pay_label: Multnomah County Circuit Court (Oregon Judicial Department)
cities.court_label: City of Portland - pay or contest a parking ticket
cities.fine_note: Oregon sets fines by statute and the court adds costs. The amount on your citation is the amount you are arguing about.
cities.school_eligible: Oregon has no statewide ticket-dismissal course. Individual courts do offer deferred sentencing or accept a course in exchange for dismissal, so the only reliable answer is the one your court gives you.
cities.points_note: Oregon does not use a point system. The DMV keeps your convictions on a driving record, and too many of them can put you into the Driver Improvement Program and cost you your licence, so the record still matters even though there are no points to count.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Oregon has no points to protect, but it does have a written-explanation trap on parking citations: sending in your explanation is a waiver of your right to a hearing.

local.h: Portland details, checked against the court and the city
bullets: Traffic citations in Portland go to the Multnomah County Circuit Court, part of the Oregon Judicial Department. Parking citations issued by the city are dealt with through the City of Portland's parking process and the same circuit court's parking office.

Parking, by mail: use the yellow envelope, a cheque or money order payable to State of Oregon (never cash), and include the citation or case number plus the licence plate. The address is Multnomah County Circuit Court, Parking Citation Office, P.O. Box 78, Portland, OR 97207.
Parking, by phone: Visa or Mastercard, on 971-274-0590, pressing option 5. Online: the Oregon Judicial Department's ePay portal, which needs your county and citation details.

The trap: sending a written explanation instead of paying is treated as a waiver of your right to a court hearing and as consent to whatever judgment the judge makes on the papers. If you want to be heard, schedule the hearing instead.

You can usually view the violation photos online before deciding - you need the citation number (near the top, starting with HA), the citation date and the plate. Photos can take up to three days to appear.

If your car was towed or booted for unpaid parking citations you must pay the full balance in guaranteed funds at the Circuit Court Customer Service Area on the second floor - and the tow company adds its own fee before releasing the car.

cities.pay_label: Salt Lake City Justice Court - online payment centre
cities.court_label: Salt Lake City Justice Court - official page
cities.fine_note: Utah publishes a uniform fine schedule, and the Justice Court posts it. That schedule - not a third-party estimate - is what your violation costs.
cities.school_eligible: Utah courts usually offer two record-saving routes instead of a plain fine: Deferred Traffic Prosecution (you pay, stay clean for the deferral period, and the charge is dismissed) and traffic school. Both are court-by-court, so ask your justice court which it runs and whether you qualify.
cities.points_note: Utah's Driver License Division assigns points by violation - a red light is 50, following too closely is 60, reckless driving is 80, and speeding runs 35 to 75 - and more than 200 points in three years can suspend your privileges (the threshold is 70 for a driver under 21).
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Salt Lake City's Justice Court gives you three doors on the same page: pay the citation, request Deferred Traffic Prosecution, or request traffic school. Taking the right one is worth more than arguing about the fine.
verify: whether your violation qualifies for Deferred Traffic Prosecution
the current uniform fine for your violation
whether the court requires an appearance for your offence

local.h: Salt Lake City details, checked against the Justice Court
bullets: Salt Lake City citations go to the Salt Lake City Justice Court at the John L. Baxter Courthouse, 333 S 200 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111.

Online: the court's own payment centre accepts a court case number, citation number or driver's licence number. Check the name on the case before you pay - the court warns about payments posted to the wrong case.
By phone: 801-535-6300, with phone hours 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday to Friday; the counter is open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
You can also schedule your arraignment and use MyCase to read your case before deciding anything - which is useful, because the court's options are not identical for every violation.
Utah's two record-saving routes are Deferred Traffic Prosecution (pay, stay clean for the deferral period, and the charge is dismissed) and traffic school. Both are offered case by case.

Points are computed by the Driver License Division: a red light is 50 points, following too closely 60, reckless driving 80, speeding 35 to 75, while more than 200 points in three years - or 70 for a driver under 21 - is what triggers a suspension.

cities.pay_label: Kansas City Municipal Court - fines, payments and sentences
cities.court_label: Missouri Case.net - look up your case
cities.fine_note: Kansas City publishes a payable-violations fine schedule and a separate court-costs table. Check your violation against the schedule before you pay, because payable and non-payable cases are treated completely differently.
cities.school_eligible: Missouri's route is the Driver Improvement Program, a state course aimed at stopping points from reaching your record and at reducing what is already there. Eligibility and the court's willingness vary, so confirm with the court or the Department of Revenue before you pay for it.
cities.points_note: Missouri's Department of Revenue sends you an advisory letter at 4 points in 12 months and suspends your driving privilege at 8 or more points in 18 months (30 days the first time, 60 the second, 90 after that). 12 points in 12 months means a one-year revocation. Points fall by a third for each clean year and reach zero after three.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: In Kansas City the first question is whether your case is payable at all. If the violation is on the court's payable fine schedule and you pay before the court date, you never go to court - if it is not, the judge decides the penalty.
verify: whether your violation is on the payable fine schedule
the exact court costs added to your fine
whether your case is in the current system or the pre-November-2023 legacy system

local.h: Kansas City details, checked against the Municipal Court
bullets: Kansas City citations go to the Kansas City Municipal Court, 511 E. 11th Street, Kansas City, MO 64106.
Online, payment runs through Missouri Case.net. Search by case number, or by name using Jackson County - 16th Judicial Circuit and then Kansas City Municipal in the court dropdown.

The rule that matters: if the case is before the court date printed on your ticket and the violation is on the court's payable fine schedule, you can pay without appearing. On non-payable cases the judge sets the penalty if you plead guilty or are found guilty.
By mail: cheque or money order payable to Municipal Court, with your name and the ticket or payment-plan number. No cash by mail.
In person: the Violations Bureau takes card, cash, cheque or money order. The lobby kiosk takes debit or credit cards, and the drop box takes cheque or money order only.
Older tickets may live in a different system: cases from before 6 November 2023 are in the legacy system, which is why a search can come back empty. Court help: 816-513-2700 or court@kcmo.org.
Missouri points come from the Department of Revenue: a warning at 4 points in 12 months, suspension at 8 or more points in 18 months, and revocation at 12 points in 12 months.

cities.pay_label: Minnesota Judicial Branch - pay a ticket
cities.court_label: Hennepin County Violations Bureau & Hearing Office
cities.fine_note: Minnesota publishes the fine for each violation, and the court adds a surcharge. The notice from the court is the amount that counts.
cities.school_eligible: Minnesota has no statewide course that removes a ticket. Many district courts do run a violations bureau hearing-officer route where you can ask for a reduction without a trial, and that is usually the cheapest thing to try.
cities.points_note: Minnesota has no point system at all. What does bite is insurance, plus the habitual-violator law: four traffic convictions in one year, or five in two years, brings a 30-day suspension (90 days for another conviction inside those windows). Minor speeding - no more than 10 over in a 55, or 5 over in a 60 - is not even recorded on your DPS driving record.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Minnesota has no points, so the argument for hiring anyone is weaker than in most states. The violations bureau hearing-officer route is the cheap first move.
verify: the current fine and surcharge for your violation
whether your case is eligible for a hearing officer
the payment address and hours for your county

local.h: Minneapolis details, checked against the Minnesota Judicial Branch
bullets: Minneapolis citations are handled by the Hennepin County District Court and its Violations Bureau & Hearing Office. The Records Center is at 300 South 6th Street, #SK-0260, Minneapolis, MN 55487-0332.
Pay online through the Minnesota Judicial Branch's pay-a-ticket service, in person with cash, card or money order, or by mail with a cheque or money order payable to Hennepin County District Court.
Minnesota has no point system. That is worth knowing before you spend money to 'keep points off' - there are none to keep off.
What does exist is the habitual violator law: four convictions in one year, or five in two years, brings a 30-day suspension - and 90 days for another conviction inside either window.
Minor speeding is not even recorded: no more than 10 mph over in a 55, or 5 over in a 60, is left off your DPS driving record.
The practical lever is the hearing officer, not a course. Ask the Violations Bureau whether your case can be heard that way - it is faster and cheaper than a trial.

cities.pay_label: Marion County Traffic Division (City of Indianapolis)
cities.court_label: Indiana MyCase - look up and manage your case
cities.fine_note: Indiana fines come with court costs, and the traffic division collects both. Check the amount on the citation or in MyCase before you pay.
cities.school_eligible: Indiana's BMV-approved defensive driving / driver safety programmes can reduce points and are often accepted by courts in place of a conviction. Which course and whether it helps is decided by the court and the BMV, so ask before you enrol.
cities.points_note: Indiana assesses points through the BMV: 14 to 18 points brings a warning letter, 20 points a one-month suspension, and it escalates from there (Indiana Administrative Code, 140 IAC 1). Reckless driving and major offences carry their own penalties.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Indianapolis traffic cases run through the Marion County Traffic Division, and you can read the whole case in MyCase before you decide anything. The due date on an Indiana ticket is short - treat the date printed on the citation as the deadline, not the date you got around to reading it.
verify: the exact due date printed on your citation
whether your offence is payable without an appearance
whether your court accepts a defensive driving course in place of a conviction

local.h: Indianapolis details, checked against the city and the state courts
bullets: Indianapolis citations are handled by the Marion County Traffic Division, which processes infractions, moving violations and traffic misdemeanours for the city.

In person: the main location is the Community Justice Campus, 675 Justice Way. There is also a counter in Room W122, City-County Building, 200 E. Washington Street. Both are open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and both take cash and cards.

By mail: a money order or cashier's cheque to Marion County Traffic Division, 200 E. Washington Street, Indianapolis, IN 46204, with a copy of the ticket. Do not mail cash, and do not assume a personal cheque will be accepted for every ticket type.
Look the case up in MyCase first. Indiana's state case system shows the charges, the hearing dates and the amount owed, and it is free.
The due date on an Indiana citation is 60 days from the day you received it. Miss it and the case can be escalated to a failure to appear, which adds costs and can affect your licence.

Indiana assesses points through the BMV: 14 to 18 points brings a warning letter and 20 points a one-month suspension, escalating from there. A BMV-approved defensive-driving course can reduce points, and courts often accept one instead of a conviction - ask before you enrol.

cities.pay_label: Colorado Springs Municipal Court - payment options, fines schedule and parking tickets
cities.court_label: Colorado Springs Municipal Court - official site (tickets, hearings, forms)
cities.school_eligible: Colorado Springs runs an Automatic Point Reduction for eligible offences: if you are charged with a traffic offence of four points or less and the officer marked your summons payable, the points are reduced automatically when you pay before the court date on the summons. Colorado itself has no course that removes points after a conviction - see the state page for the deferral and DMV hearing route.
cities.points_note: Colorado suspends an adult driver at 12 points in 12 months, and points stay on your record two years from the offence. Paying the summons is a guilty plea unless your charge qualifies for the Automatic Point Reduction.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.fine_note: The court publishes a schedule of payable fines and bail, and the officer marks the payable amount on the front of the summons. If no amount is printed, the summons is not payable and you must appear. Parking tickets must be paid within 14 days, with a $5 late charge added on the 15th day.
verify: whether the exact charge on your summons is a city-code violation (Municipal Court) or a state charge (El Paso County Court)
the payable fine/bail amount printed on your summons, or the current schedule of payable fines
whether your offence is four points or less, so the Automatic Point Reduction applies

local.h: Colorado Springs details, verified against the City's Municipal Court
bullets: Your ticket is handled by the Colorado Springs Municipal Court, which hears violations of the city code, including city traffic offences - court home page. If a state trooper charged you under state law instead, that case goes to El Paso County Court, not this court - check the issuing agency on the ticket.
Start from the court's own payment page. It lists the schedule of payable fines, the online payment portal and the parking-ticket rules - there is no other official payment site for these tickets.

The city's best-kept deal is the Automatic Point Reduction. If your charge is four points or less and payable, and you pay before the court date on your summons, the points come off automatically - no course, no hearing. Paying is otherwise a guilty plea that sends points to the DMV.
If you are contesting the charge or pleading not guilty, you must appear on the court date. Paying instead means you give up that right, so do not pay if you intend to fight it.

The court also runs a Remote Disposition process with the City Attorney's prosecution division: qualifying cases can be resolved without coming in, but only for defendants who live outside El Paso County or need a disability accommodation, and the request must be submitted at least 10 days before the court date.

Two phone numbers worth keeping: the court is 719-385-5922 (hours Mon-Fri, 8am-4pm; email MunicipalCourtViolations@ColoradoSprings.Gov), and probation is 719-385-5923. Allow 24 hours for a reply to messages.

Parking tickets are on a different clock. Pay within 14 days or a $5 late charge is added on the 15th day; to contest one, see a Court Referee rather than a judge. Parking is also payable on the separate nCourt portal linked from the payment page.
If a payment is missed the city warns of added costs and even an arrest warrant, so if you cannot pay, contact the court about options rather than going silent.

cities.pay_label: Hillsborough Clerk of Court - pay a traffic ticket (online 24/7, phone, mail, in person)
cities.court_label: Hillsborough County Clerk of Courts - Traffic Department
cities.school_eligible: Florida lets you elect a 4-hour Basic Driver Improvement course. If you pay for it and complete it, adjudication is withheld and the DMV assesses no points, and your insurer cannot raise your rate or cancel you. Hillsborough allows the election once in a 12-month period and no more than five times in your lifetime; a CDL or commercial-vehicle ticket cannot use it.
cities.points_note: Florida adds 3, 4 or 6 points per moving violation and suspends at 12 points in 12 months, 18 in 18, or 24 in 36. Points stay on your record three years - which is why the school election matters more than the fine.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.fine_note: The fine comes from Florida's statewide penalty schedule plus county surcharges and is printed on your citation. Paying the civil penalty is an admission of guilt and the DMV will assess points for a moving violation.
verify: the exact deadline on your citation (Hillsborough gives 60 calendar days to pay, from the issue date)
whether your violation is eligible for the Basic Driver Improvement election
the payable amount and any county surcharge printed on your citation

local.h: Tampa / Hillsborough County details, verified against the Clerk of Courts
bullets: Your ticket is a county case, collected by the Hillsborough County Clerk of Courts (Victor D. Crist) for the 13th Judicial Circuit - Traffic Department. A Tampa police or sheriff's officer writes the ticket, but the Clerk handles payment, the school election and hearings.

Two clocks run at once. You have 30 calendar days to tell the Clerk how you want to resolve the ticket (pay, elect school, or request a hearing). After that your only option is to pay and take the points. Separately you have 60 calendar days to actually pay and finish every requirement.

No extension is available. The Clerk already built a 30-day extension into the 60-day figure, so it will not grant another one. If you cannot comply within 60 days, the move is to request a court hearing, not to let it lapse - late payment raises the penalty and can suspend your licence.
Look your ticket up or pay it on the Clerk's own pages: look up a ticket and paying for tickets. Pay online 24/7 or by phone 24/7 at 813-276-8100 (have your ticket and Florida licence/ID ready).

Other ways to pay: by mail with a personal check, cashier's check or money order to Clerk of the Circuit Court - Traffic, PO Box 3360, Tampa FL 33601-3360 (include a copy of the ticket), or in cash at Amscot locations and at Clerk offices Monday-Friday. Credit cards carry a 3.5% transaction fee.
Only the driver's own credit card can pay a driver's ticket, and the billing ZIP must match, or the charge fails and a hold is placed on the funds for up to 10 business days.

The school election is the big lever. It keeps the ticket off your record, stops points and blocks an insurance increase - but the completion certificate from the school must reach the Clerk within 60 calendar days of the issue date, with no extension. See the Clerk's traffic school page.

To contest it instead, request a court hearing through the Clerk within the 30-day window. A city of Tampa ticket and a Hillsborough County ticket both land here - the issuing agency does not change the court.

cities.pay_label: Duval County Clerk of Courts - pay a traffic citation online (ePay)
cities.court_label: Duval County Clerk of Courts - Traffic (citations and options)
cities.school_eligible: Jacksonville uses the Florida Basic Driver Improvement election: pay the citation in full and complete the school, and adjudication is withheld so the DMV assesses no points. Florida allows it once in a 12-month period and no more than five times in your lifetime, and a CDL or commercial-vehicle ticket cannot use it.
cities.points_note: Florida adds 3, 4 or 6 points per moving violation and suspends at 12 points in 12 months, 18 in 18, or 24 in 36. Paying the citation is a conviction and the points go on your record, so the school election is the decision that matters.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.fine_note: The fine comes from Florida's statewide penalty schedule plus county surcharges and is printed on your citation. The Duval Clerk collects it - paying is a conviction and points are assessed for a moving violation.
verify: your citation's issue date (you have 30 days to respond) and the payable amount printed on it
whether your violation is eligible for the Driver Improvement School election
the courthouse and hearing details if you choose to contest the citation

local.h: Jacksonville / Duval County details, verified against the Clerk of Courts
bullets: Jacksonville is a consolidated city-county, so your citation goes to the Duval County Clerk of the Circuit Court (Jody Phillips) for the 4th Judicial Circuit - Traffic department. Jacksonville Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol tickets all land here.

You have 30 calendar days from the issue date to respond. Miss it and - in the Clerk's own words - your licence will be suspended and extra fees added. The three options are on the ticket itself: pay, pay and elect Driver Improvement School, or request a court date.

Paying is a conviction. If you pay the civil citation, points are assessed and you can no longer switch to the school option later. If points are your concern, do not pay first and ask questions after.
Everything is on the Clerk's site: pay online through ePay, read the traffic-citation payment page, or pull the traffic forms if you are responding by mail.

The Driver Improvement election lets you keep the ticket off your record even though you pay it - you pay in full and complete the school, and adjudication is withheld with no points. Florida allows it once in 12 months, max five times in a lifetime, and never for a CDL holder.
To fight the ticket, request a court date within the 30-day window rather than paying. The hearing is your chance to contest the officer's account; a paid ticket cannot be reopened.

If you were charged with a criminal traffic offence (DUI, reckless driving, driving on a suspended licence), that is not a civil citation and the options on this page do not apply - you need the criminal case, and usually a lawyer.
One caution: Duval's Clerk system is shared with civil and criminal filings, so always confirm the case number matches your citation before you pay.

cities.pay_label: Hamilton County Clerk of Courts - look up and pay court costs / traffic tickets online
cities.court_label: Hamilton County Clerk of Courts - traffic ticket search, payout amounts and online payment
cities.school_eligible: Ohio's record tool is a 2-point credit for completing a BMV-approved remedial driving course. It is a credit against your point total rather than a dismissal, so confirm what Cincinnati Municipal Court and the BMV will accept before you pay for a course - see the state page.
cities.points_note: Ohio assesses points on conviction and 12 points in two years triggers a 12-point suspension (a class-D suspension that typically runs six months). Points stay on your record two years from the conviction.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.fine_note: Fines and court costs vary by violation, and many Ohio courts only show an online payment button once the case is marked payable. Treat the amount printed on your court notice as the real number.
verify: the exact case number and payable amount for your ticket in the Clerk's lookup
whether your offence is one where a remedial driving course is accepted for a point credit
the Cincinnati Municipal Court date and courtroom printed on your notice

local.h: Cincinnati / Hamilton County details, verified against the Clerk of Courts
bullets: Your ticket is handled by the Hamilton County Clerk of Courts (Pavan V. Parikh), the record keeper for the Cincinnati Municipal Court - see the Clerk's Traffic Tickets page. Cincinnati Police moving-violation tickets are entered here.

The Clerk's traffic page gives you three things in one place: a traffic ticket search, the payout amounts for Hamilton County moving violations, and online payment. Cincinnati Municipal Court is the court of record for city tickets.

Look up the case before you pay. Use the Clerk's court costs / ticket search to confirm your case number and the exact amount - Ohio court costs are itemised and can differ from the number you remember from the ticket.

The Clerk's own caveat matters: the listings reflect only records already entered in the database. Tickets issued by Cincinnati Police Records or others may be open but not yet listed, so a search that returns nothing does not mean you have no ticket.
Parking is separate. City of Cincinnati parking tickets go through the city's parking violations process, not the Clerk's traffic division - check the issuing authority on the ticket.

Ohio uses points, not traffic school. Convictions add points and 12 points in two years triggers a class-D suspension; a BMV-approved remedial driving course credits 2 points against the total. It reduces points rather than erasing the ticket, so check first.
More serious charges (DUI/OVI, driving under suspension) are criminal matters in Cincinnati Municipal Court and are not resolvable with a simple online payment - those usually need a lawyer.
If you want to contest the ticket, do not pay first. Ask the Clerk for the case schedule and appear for the arraignment; paying is treated as a no-contest or guilty plea.

cities.pay_label: Spokane Municipal Court - eCourt Portal (look up and pay tickets online)
cities.court_label: Spokane Municipal Court - respond to a ticket (infractions, hearings, forms)
cities.school_eligible: Washington has no traffic-school dismissal. The equivalent is a deferred finding: the court defers the ticket for up to a year and, if you stay violation-free, it never goes on your record. Most drivers get one deferral for a moving and one for a non-moving infraction every seven years - ask about it before you pay.
cities.points_note: Washington does not use points. A civil infraction still shows on your DOL record for three years and can affect your insurance - a deferred finding keeps it off, which is the real prize.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.fine_note: Washington sets a statewide penalty schedule for civil traffic infractions, so the base fine is the same across the state. The amount is printed on your notice, plus any local assessments.
verify: whether your notice is a Spokane Municipal Court infraction or a Spokane County District Court one
the 30-day response deadline and the option you select on the ticket
whether your infraction is eligible for a deferred finding

local.h: Spokane details, verified against the City's Municipal Court
bullets: Spokane has two ticket courts: the Spokane Municipal Court (city tickets, founded 2009) and Spokane County District Court (county and state infractions). Read the court name on your notice - a city officer's ticket goes to Municipal Court, and everything below is the Municipal Court process. Tickets page.

You must respond within 30 days of the issue date. Select one of the options printed on the ticket and return it to the Municipal Court Clerk's Office by mail or in person - if you mail it, it must be postmarked by midnight on the due day.

The penalty for silence is steep: if you fail to respond or to appear, the court enters a finding of committed for the full fine, adds a $52 fee, and refers the account to a collection agency. For a traffic infraction it also notifies the state.

Your two hearing choices are a contested hearing (dispute that you committed the infraction) or a mitigation hearing (admit it but explain circumstances to seek a reduced fine). You can appear in person or submit a written statement instead, using the court's contest or mitigate form.
Pay online through the eCourt Portal, or by mail to 1100 W. Mallon, Spokane, WA 99260. The payments page also lists the full fee schedule and payment plans.

Payment plans exist for traffic and code infractions: sign an agreement at the Clerk's Office, send a signed written request by mail, or ask the judicial officer for a plan at your contested or mitigation hearing. It is a better move than defaulting.

The real prize in Washington is a deferred finding, not a fine reduction: ask the court to defer the ticket for up to a year, stay clean, and it never reaches your record or your insurer. Most drivers get one deferred finding for a moving and one for a non-moving infraction every seven years.

Criminal misdemeanour tickets (DUI, driving while suspended) are different: an officer usually writes an arraignment date on the face of the ticket and you must appear, or a warrant will issue. Those cases belong with the criminal calendar, not the infraction process.

cities.pay_label: Kern County Superior Court - make a payment online
cities.court_label: Kern County Superior Court - Traffic Court (process, school, red light, failure to appear)
cities.school_eligible: Kern County runs California's Traffic Violator School (TVS). If your violation is eligible, completing an approved school keeps a point off your DMV record - and since AB 2499 the court can no longer dismiss the ticket, so only your first conviction in an 18-month period is kept confidential. A CDL holder cited in a non-commercial vehicle may still attend, but the conviction is not masked.
cities.points_note: A moving violation adds a point to your DMV record and can raise your insurance for up to three years, so the school election is usually worth more than the fine.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.fine_note: Fines vary by violation and county. Kern publishes its own fee and fine payment options - the amount on your Courtesy Notice is the real number.
verify: the fine amount or mandatory-appearance date on your Courtesy Notice (it should arrive at least 10 days before the appearance date)
whether your violation is eligible for Traffic Violator School
whether a payment plan or an Ability-to-Pay reduction applies to you

local.h: Bakersfield / Kern County details, verified against Kern County Superior Court
bullets: Kern County traffic goes to the Superior Court of California, County of Kern - start from the court's own Traffic Court page. There is no separate city traffic court; a Bakersfield police or CHP ticket lands here.

Watch for the Courtesy Notice. Within a few weeks of the citation the court mails a Courtesy Notice showing your fine amount, or a mandatory-appearance date and time. It should arrive at least 10 days before the appearance date - if it never shows up, appear on or before the date printed on your citation anyway.

Paying is a guilty plea. Pay online through the court's payment page or follow the options on the notice. If your citation requires a mandatory court appearance, a fine payment alone will not close the case.

Traffic Violator School is the record fix, once every 18 months on an eligible violation. See the court's Traffic School page; since AB 2499 the ticket is still recorded, but your first conviction in 18 months is kept confidential and no point is assessed.
If money is the problem, Kern points you to the statewide MyCitations tool and its Can’t Afford to Pay page - both can reduce or spread the fine rather than force a default.
Do not simply ignore it. The court has a dedicated Failure to Appear or Pay page: a missed date adds a civil assessment and can suspend your licence, and it escalates fast.
Parking is not the Traffic Division's. Kern says to contact the law-enforcement agency printed on the parking ticket, and traffic-court lawyers are separate: DUI goes to the Criminal Department.

cities.pay_label: Broward County Clerk of Courts - pay a traffic citation (eServices / online payment)
cities.court_label: Broward County Clerk of Courts - Traffic & Misdemeanor division
cities.school_eligible: Florida lets you elect a 4-hour Basic Driver Improvement course. Complete it and adjudication is withheld, no points reach the DMV, and your insurer cannot raise or cancel your policy. Florida allows the election once in a 12-month period and no more than five times in your lifetime, and a CDL or commercial-vehicle ticket cannot use it.
cities.points_note: Florida adds 3, 4 or 6 points per moving violation and suspends at 12 points in 12 months, 18 in 18, or 24 in 36. Points stay on your record three years, so the school election matters more than the fine.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.fine_note: The fine comes from Florida's statewide penalty schedule plus Broward County surcharges, printed on your citation. The Clerk collects it; paying is a conviction and points are assessed for a moving violation.
verify: the response and payment deadlines printed on your citation
whether your violation is eligible for the Basic Driver Improvement election
the exact payable amount, including Broward County surcharges

local.h: Fort Lauderdale / Broward County details, verified against the Clerk of Courts
bullets: Broward County citations are handled by the Broward County Clerk of Courts for the 17th Judicial Circuit - see the Traffic & Misdemeanor division. A Fort Lauderdale police or Broward Sheriff's deputy writes the ticket; the Clerk collects it.

Florida's two clocks: you have roughly 30 calendar days to tell the Clerk how you want to resolve the ticket (pay, elect school, or request a hearing), and 60 calendar days to actually pay and finish the requirements. Blowing either one raises the penalty and can suspend your licence.

Paying is a conviction. If you pay the civil penalty, points go on your record for a moving violation - and under Florida law you cannot switch to the school option later. Decide which way you are going before you pay.

Look up and pay on the Clerk's site: Pay a Traffic Citation or read the Pay Fines and Fees and Elect Driving School sections of the Traffic & Misdemeanor page. The Clerk also runs a Driver License Check so you can see what is on your record.

The Basic Driver Improvement election is the record fix: pay in full, complete the 4-hour course, and adjudication is withheld with no points. Once per 12 months, max five times in a lifetime, never for a CDL holder.
To fight it, request a court hearing within the response window instead of paying - a paid ticket cannot be reopened later.
Parking is separate. Broward parking citations run through the Clerk's Parking division and the agency that issued them, not the traffic division.

Scam warning: the Clerk posts an FLHSMV payment scam alert - phony sites and texts impersonate Florida traffic portals. Always reach the payment page by typing the Clerk's own domain, not a link from a text message.

cities.pay_label: Reno Municipal Court - payments (post and forfeit, payment plans)
cities.court_label: Reno Municipal Court - traffic citations (civil infractions vs criminal violations)
cities.school_eligible: Nevada does not dismiss a ticket with a course, but the DMV gives a 3-point demerit reduction for a DMV-approved traffic safety course when you have 3-11 active points, generally once every 12 months. A course taken under a court plea agreement does not earn that reduction, so ask the clerk exactly which route your citation allows.
cities.points_note: Nevada counts demerit points: 12 or more in a 12-month period can suspend your licence. A civil infraction conviction still reports to the DMV, so paying is not a way to keep the record clean.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.fine_note: Nevada splits citations into civil infractions and criminal traffic offences, and the fine depends on the violation and the court. The citation shows your response date - Reno gives civil infractions 90 days to respond.
verify: whether your citation is a civil infraction or a criminal traffic offence, and whether it is a mandatory-appearance violation
the fine, fees and assessments on your case (the court's chat line can quote them)
the 90-day response date for a civil infraction before a default judgment is entered

local.h: Reno / Washoe County details, verified against Reno Municipal Court
bullets: Reno citations go to the Reno Municipal Court, not a county court - start from the court's Traffic Citations page. Read the citation first: Nevada now separates civil infractions from criminal traffic offences, and they follow different routes.

Civil infractions get 90 days to respond. If you take no action by the 90-day response date, the court enters a default judgment: you are found in violation, fines and penalties are assessed, and the case can no longer be contested.

Paying early is called a ‘Post and Forfeit’ - and it means exactly what it says. By paying before your hearing you waive the right to a hearing, admit guilt, and a conviction is reported to the DMV. You cannot later change your plea or undo the conviction, and it is not the same as posting bail.
Pay, request a new arraignment date or find your case through the court's Payments page. For bail, bond or a fine quote, call a court clerk at (775) 334-2290, option 6, or use the court's chat line.
If any violation is a mandatory appearance (noted next to the violation on the ticket), you must appear in person at the time listed - paying will not substitute for the hearing.

The court offers payment plans if you cannot pay in full by the hearing date, and a Virtual Clerk Counter open Monday-Thursday, 8:30-11:30 a.m. and 2:00-5:00 p.m., so you can handle routine business without going to the courthouse.

For the record, not just the fine: ask whether a DMV-approved traffic safety course can cut 3 demerit points from your total (3-11 active points, once a year) - and confirm it is not a court-ordered course, which does not earn the reduction.
DUI is a criminal traffic offence at this court, handled on the criminal calendar with a mandatory appearance - not something a fine payment resolves.

cities.court_label: Akron Municipal Court - Traffic / Parking (waivers, walk-ins, court dates)

cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.fine_note: Fines and court costs vary by violation. For a waiver ticket the amount is set for you; for anything else Akron Municipal Court only shows a payable balance once the case is marked payable.

local.h: Akron / Summit County details, verified against Akron Municipal Court
bullets: Akron tickets are handled by the Akron Municipal Court - start from the court's Traffic / Parking page. Traffic Court is staffed by a full-time magistrate, a bailiff, a traffic safety officer and a traffic clerk.

Check whether your ticket is a ‘waiver’. A waiver means you can pay without coming to court. Look up your case and pay the balance on the court's portal (case search and pay a fine), or pay in person or by mail. For the exact amount, call the Clerk of Court - Traffic Division at (330) 375-2572.

Walk-ins are Monday-Thursday at 9 a.m. or 1 p.m. - there are no Friday walk-ins. Traffic Court sits Monday-Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and closes 12-1 p.m. for lunch. If your ticket requires an appearance, appear on or before the date on the ticket.
You cannot move a traffic date by phone. Akron says any request to change a court date must be made in writing as a Motion for Request - so a quick call will not buy you more time.
If you have a waiver ticket and want a payment plan, you must still appear in Traffic Court on or before the date on the ticket; a plan is not something you can set up purely online.

The Clerk of Court - Criminal, Traffic & Parking Division handles the paperwork, and the court moved to a new electronic case-management system in September 2025, so if a link or balance looks off, call the Traffic Division rather than assuming the ticket is gone.

For the record: an Ohio conviction adds points, and 12 points in two years triggers a class-D suspension. A BMV-approved remedial driving course credits 2 points against your total - it reduces points, it does not erase the ticket.

cities.court_label: Dayton Municipal Court - official site

cities.points_note: Ohio assesses points on conviction and 12 points in two years triggers a 12-point suspension (a class-D suspension, typically six months). Points stay on your record two years from the conviction.

local.h: Dayton / Montgomery County details, verified against Dayton Municipal Court
bullets: Dayton city tickets go to the Dayton Municipal Court - start from the court's own site at daytonmunicipalcourt.org. Search your case and find payment through the Clerk of Court portal at clerkofcourt.daytonohio.gov.

The Clerk portal is organised by type: Traffic & Criminal, Photo Enforcement, Parking, Jury, and a Civil Docket. Pick the right tab - traffic and photo-enforcement notices follow different payment paths.
Court contact is (937) 333-4338. Downloadable forms - including the Traffic & Criminal forms - are on the Clerk's site if you are filing or responding by mail.

Do not confuse the courts. Dayton Municipal Court handles city tickets; Montgomery County courts (via montcourt.oh.gov) handle county-level cases. Check the court name on your citation before you act.

Photo-enforcement and parking notices are their own thing. If your notice came in the mail from a camera or a parking system, treat it as that type of notice and use the matching tab, not the traffic case search.

For the record: an Ohio conviction adds points, 12 points in two years triggers a class-D suspension, and a BMV-approved remedial driving course credits 2 points against the total rather than dismissing the ticket.
The Clerk's site also carries the official Ohio court links and forms, so if you are self-represented you can find the traffic forms and the case schedule without going through a third-party site.

cities.court_label: Tacoma Municipal Court - traffic & parking infractions (mitigation vs contested)
cities.school_eligible: Washington has no traffic-school dismissal. Most drivers get one deferral for a moving and one for a non-moving infraction every seven years - ask about it before you pay.

local.h: Tacoma / Pierce County details, verified against Tacoma Municipal Court
bullets: City tickets in Tacoma go to the Tacoma Municipal Court, a court of limited jurisdiction over city-ordinance cases - start from the court's Traffic & Parking Infractions page.

Respond on time or lose options. You have a set number of days to respond to the ticket in person, and 33 days if the Notice of Infraction came by mail. Responding means either paying the penalty or requesting a court date - silence leads to a committed finding and collections.

Two hearings, two goals. A mitigation hearing is for when you agree you committed the infraction but want to explain the circumstances - the judge will not dismiss it but may reduce the penalty. A contested hearing is for when you believe you did not commit it: you may testify, present evidence and call witnesses, and the ticket can be dismissed.

Subpoena the officer if you are contesting. Unless you request that the officer (or radar technician) be present, the judge simply reads the officer's sworn statement. Tell the clerk when you schedule if you want them there.
There is no public defender for infractions. You may hire an attorney at your own expense, but traffic and parking infractions do not qualify for appointed counsel.

Pay through the court's online portal (pay a ticket, fine or fee) or by mail to 930 Tacoma Avenue South, Room 841, Tacoma, WA 98402. Note: court-date requests are not accepted by phone - sign the back of the ticket and mail it, or file through the court.
Watch for scams. Tacoma Municipal Court states plainly that no member of the court will ever call you to ask for payment or card details - so any such call is fraudulent.

The real prize is a deferred finding: ask the court to defer the infraction up to a year and, if you stay clean, it never reaches your record or insurer. Ask before paying, because paying is a committed finding.

cities.court_label: Knox County Courts - General Sessions (Criminal & Traffic), Criminal, Circuit, Chancery
cities.school_eligible: Tennessee has two routes: a court-ordered traffic school can get a citation dismissed if the judge allows it, and separately the Department of Safety will remove up to 5 points from a speeding conviction if you complete an approved 4-hour driver education course. Course providers must send your certificate to the Department within 30 days, so ask the school who files it.
cities.points_note: Tennessee's Department of Safety runs a driver-improvement point system: 12 points in 12 months can bring a proposed suspension and a hearing. Points stay on your record for years, and the insurance effect usually costs more than the fine.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.fine_note: Fines and court costs vary by violation. Check the court's current fine schedule, and treat the amount printed on your court notice as the real number.

local.h: Knoxville / Knox County details, verified against Knox County courts
bullets: Knoxville is the seat of Knox County, which runs several courts - see the county's Court System page. Moving and traffic citations are handled by the General Sessions Court - Criminal and Traffic, whose records sit with the Knox County Criminal Court Clerk.

The Criminal Court Clerk's office files and keeps the records for the Criminal Court, General Sessions Criminal, and Fourth Circuit Courts. Clerk Mike Hammond's office is at the City County Building and can be reached at (865) 215-2375 - see the Clerk's site.

Pay or manage your case through KnoxCourtPay, the Clerk's official app and online service, and use the same site to find your court date and today's dockets. Reach it from the Clerk's page rather than a search result, to avoid look-alike sites.

The Clerk's office does more than take money. It handles driver's-licence reinstatement, expungement screenings and criminal background searches - useful if your ticket snowballed into a licence problem.

Knox County also runs Chancery, Circuit, Fourth Circuit, Civil Sessions and Juvenile courts; if your citation or a related matter is set in one of those, use the matching court page rather than the General Sessions traffic process.

Tennessee's record fix is twofold: a judge can let a court-ordered traffic school dismiss a citation, and a state-approved 4-hour driver-education course removes up to 5 points from a speeding conviction. The school must file your certificate within 30 days - confirm who files it.

Points matter more than the fine: 12 points in 12 months can trigger a proposed licence suspension and a hearing, and the insurance increase outlasts the ticket. If your licence is at risk, ask about school before you pay.

local.h: Santa Ana details, verified against Orange County Superior Court
bullets: A Santa Ana citation is filed with the Superior Court of California, County of Orange, Traffic Division. Santa Ana cases are heard at the Central Justice Center, 700 Civic Center Dr. West, Santa Ana - the courthouse printed on your citation is the one that decides your case, and Orange County has four Criminal & Traffic departments (Central in Santa Ana, Harbor in Newport Beach, North in Fullerton, West in Westminster).

Pay online through My Court Portal (payment, extension, payment plan, proof of correction, case reminders). If you pay through the older OC Pay system you need the OC Pay # printed on the citation, and that route only works on or before your original due date - after that, use My Court Portal.

By mail: check or money order only (never cash), payable to Clerk of the Court, with the case or citation number written on it, to Information Payment Center, P.O. Box 6040, Newport Beach, CA 92658-6040. Online payment takes Visa, MasterCard, Discover, American Express, EFT and debit.

Extensions the clerk can grant without a judge: one 45-day extension plus a second 30-day extension before any failure-to-appear action, and a further 30 days to finish traffic school once the school fine and fees are paid.

You can also post bail, enrol in traffic school and request an extension through the court's automated phone system. Internet payments cannot be used to post bail for a court trial or a trial by written declaration - those need the clerk.

Traffic school: valid California licence, no traffic school in the last 18 months, and the violation must not require a mandatory appearance. Check the DMV's approved-school list through selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/traffic/traffic-school.

Cannot afford the fine? Ask for an ability-to-pay determination on MyCitations - Orange County can lower the amount, set a payment plan or allow community service, but ask before the due date, not after.
Parking tickets are not court cases in Santa Ana - they are handled by the City of Santa Ana parking enforcement, and the court will not accept payment for them.
Missing the date is the expensive part: a failure to appear brings a DMV hold and a civil assessment on top of the fine. See the court's appearances and failure-to-appear page.

verify: the bail amount for your specific violation (Orange County sets it per violation and the number on your notice is the real one)
whether your citation allows online handling - some Orange County violations require a mandatory court appearance
cities.tool_note: Santa Ana is served by the Central Justice Center on Civic Center Drive West; Huntington Beach, Westminster and Garden Grove tickets go to the West Justice Center instead.

local.h: Huntington Beach details, verified against Orange County Superior Court
bullets: Huntington Beach tickets do not go to Santa Ana. They are filed with the Superior Court of California, County of Orange and heard at the West Justice Center, 8141 13th Street, Westminster - check the courthouse named on your citation before you drive anywhere.

Payment, extensions, payment plans, proof of correction and case reminders all run through My Court Portal. Online payment needs your OC Pay # and only works on or before your original due date (OC Pay).
By mail: check or money order (no cash), payable to Clerk of the Court, with the case or citation number on it, to Information Payment Center, P.O. Box 6040, Newport Beach, CA 92658-6040.
The clerk can grant one 45-day extension and a second 30-day extension before any failure-to-appear action, plus 30 days to complete traffic school once the school fees are paid.

Traffic school needs a valid California licence, no traffic school in the last 18 months, and no mandatory-appearance violation; the officer's discretion governs if you were found guilty at trial. Approved schools: selfhelp.courts.ca.gov.
Financial hardship is an option, not a favour: request an ability-to-pay determination on MyCitations for a lower fine, a payment plan or community service.

Beach parking is the local trap. Parking and beach-lot citations in Huntington Beach are issued by the City of Huntington Beach, not the court - they are paid to and appealed through the city, and unpaid ones can block your registration renewal.
Court trials and trials by written declaration cannot be paid online, and internet payment cannot be used to post bail - go through the clerk for those.

the current bail amount for your violation (Orange County sets it per violation, not per city)
cities.tool_note: If your ticket was written by a Huntington Beach officer, the courthouse is the West Justice Center in Westminster - not the Central Justice Center that serves Santa Ana.

local.h: San Bernardino details, verified against San Bernardino Superior Court
bullets: San Bernardino County is one court with several district locations (San Bernardino, Fontana, Victorville, Barstow, Needles, Big Bear). Your citation names the district, and that is where your case lives - the county traffic page lists which options each district allows.
Pay through Pay a Traffic Ticket - the county's own payment page - or in person at the courthouse on your ticket. The court also publishes a payment FAQ if the portal rejects your case number.

Correctable violations are the exception. A fix-it violation (registration, licence, insurance, equipment) cannot be paid online unless you pay the full amount without showing proof of correction. If you want the reduced fee, show the signed-off citation or proof to the court instead of paying on the website.

The reminder notice is a courtesy, not a deadline: the court says if you do not receive it, you are still responsible for handling the case by the appearance date printed on the citation. If you have no notice within two weeks of that date, contact the clerk.

Traffic school information, eligibility and fees are on the court's own Traffic School Information page - San Bernardino allows a parent or guardian to attend school with a minor in some cases, so read the county page rather than assuming.
Big Bear District citations can be handled by remote video proceedings instead of driving up the mountain - ask the clerk for the remote appearance option.
If you want a court date, you must call the clerk's office listed on your ticket to reserve one; you cannot simply show up.
Doing nothing is the worst option: the court states that missing the appearance date can add extra fees, put a hold on your driver's licence and send the case to collections.

Pay and manage the case through the county's Traffic Division page, which links the payment portal, the traffic school request and the contest options. Online payment works on or before the due date; after that the clerk's options shrink.

Riverside County courts accept payment online by credit or debit card, by mail with a check or money order, in person at the traffic window, and through the drop boxes at the courthouses. Never send cash.

Proof of correction (fix-it) tickets: the reduced fee applies only if the correctable violation is signed off and shown to the court - paying the full amount online closes the case as a conviction instead.

Traffic school: California allows it once every 18 months for an eligible violation with a valid licence and no mandatory appearance. Riverside County route: request it through the court (the traffic school fee is added), then choose a school from the DMV's approved list via selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/traffic/traffic-school.

Financial hardship: the county points drivers to MyCitations for a reduced fine, a payment plan, community service or more time to pay. The application is for infractions only and the court can revisit the decision if your situation changes.

Parking tickets are handled by the city that issued them (Riverside, Corona, Moreno Valley and so on), not by the Superior Court - and a city parking ticket and a court citation are two different cases.
If the case goes to failure to appear, expect a civil assessment and a DMV hold; the court's traffic page explains how to clear a hold once the case is resolved.

Cost trouble? MyCitations is the county's route to a lower fine, a payment plan or community service. It covers infractions, and the earlier you ask the more options you have.
Ignoring the citation is what turns a fine into a licence hold: a failure to appear adds a civil assessment and a DMV hold, and clearing it later costs more than the original bail.

Traffic school: valid California licence, no traffic school in the last 18 months, no mandatory-appearance violation, and if you were found guilty at trial the judge decides. Confiscation of the point is the prize, not the course itself - approved schools are listed via selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/traffic/traffic-school.
Financial hardship is an explicit option in San Joaquin: ask the court to reduce the amount based on your ability to pay through MyCitations.

The court does not guarantee you a reminder: if you never receive the notice, it is still your responsibility to find the fine amount, hearing date and payment due date, and to deal with the case.

Not the driver? If the citation came to you as the registered owner and someone else was driving, do not pay it - complete the affidavit of non-liability section on the notice of violation. Paying first usually means giving up that option.
Alameda County is a big court with several locations; the county's traffic page and your citation's courthouse line are the only reliable guide to where your case sits.

bullets: Modesto is the seat of the Superior Court of California, County of Stanislaus, and traffic is handled at the Traffic Division, 2260 Floyd Avenue, Modesto, CA 95355, (209) 530-3100, open weekdays from 8:15 a.m. The court also answers traffic questions by e-mail at Traffic.Requests@stanct.org.

Civil assessment: California capped it at $100 from 1 July 2022 (it was $300), and pre-July-2022 civil assessment debt was cancelled. If you are paying an old case in full, the court says to exclude any civil assessment balance from before 30 June 2022 - ask the clerk rather than overpaying.

A trial by written declaration requires you to post bail in advance (check, cashier's check or card) - and it cannot be paid through the website. Send the case number with every payment and allow two days for an online payment to process.

Traffic school and proof-of-correction violations need the court's sign-off rather than an online payment; the county's MyCitations tool handles ability-to-pay requests, payment plans, more time, or community service in lieu of fines for eligible infractions.

A licence hold is the usual consequence of failing to appear on an Oxnard ticket - the county says plainly that failure to appear can put a hold on your driver's licence, and only the Juvenile Courthouse can clear a juvenile hold.
Monthly payment arrangements run through MyCitations, and the same tool handles an ability-to-pay reduction; the county also points hardship cases at its MyCitations page.

local.h: Santa Rosa details, verified against Sonoma County Superior Court

Extensions are quick here: request one through the Pay Online link, or call (707) 521-6680 between 8:00 a.m. and noon, Monday to Friday. The case still has to be cleared on or before the due date (or the extension you were granted).

Traffic violator school is worth understanding in Sonoma: one conviction in any 18-month period stays confidential on your DMV record if you complete a school and pay the school fees. Approved schools are listed through selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/traffic/traffic-school.

Insurance violations (VC 16028) are dismissed only if you show or mail evidence of financial responsibility that was valid on the date the citation was issued, plus the transaction fee on your notice - proof bought after the stop does not clear it.

A missed due date in Sonoma brings a stack: a $100 civil assessment under Penal Code 1214.1, penalties and fees, a hold or suspension on your licence, and possibly a warrant. Ability-to-pay alternatives (payment plan, community service) run through MyCitations.

local.h: Fairfield details, verified against Solano County Superior Court
bullets: Fairfield is the seat of the Superior Court of California, County of Solano, which handles all Solano traffic citations through its Traffic Court - the courthouse written on your citation is the one that owns the case (the county runs locations in Fairfield and Vallejo).

Pay through the court's Traffic Court page, which links the payment options, the traffic school request and the ability-to-pay route. The page also answers the question drivers actually ask: what happens if the citation is not cleared by the court's due date.

Financial hardship has a formal path here. Solano County tells you to ask the court to consider your ability to pay the underlying fine by filing a completed Declaration / Ability to Pay form - and it states that a release of the hold on your driver's licence is issued once the court decides on your declaration, which is the part that matters if a hold is already on your record.
Expect a civil assessment on top of the fine if the case goes delinquent; California caps it at $100 and that is the number Solano applies.

Traffic school: valid California licence, no traffic school in the last 18 months, no mandatory-appearance violation, and the judicial officer's discretion if you were found guilty at trial. Approved schools: selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/traffic/traffic-school.

Everything is easier before the due date: extensions are granted by the clerk on request, but once a case is past due the clerk's authority shrinks and the file is closer to collections and licence action.
If you were cited by the California Highway Patrol on I-80 or I-680, the citation is still filed with the Solano County court named on it - the issuing agency does not change the court.
Fairfield and Vallejo parking tickets are city matters, handled by the issuing city and not by the Superior Court.

cities.tool_note: Solano County ties its ability-to-pay declaration directly to releasing a driver's-licence hold - filing it is how you get a hold lifted.

local.h: Vallejo details, verified against Solano County Superior Court
bullets: A Vallejo ticket is filed with the Superior Court of California, County of Solano. The county runs its traffic operation out of Fairfield and Vallejo - check the courthouse on your citation before driving to the wrong one across the county.

Payment, extensions, traffic school requests and hardship declarations all start from the court's Traffic Court page, which the county keeps current on what happens when a citation is not cleared by the due date.
If a licence hold has already been placed, the county's stated route is an Ability to Pay / Declaration form: the release of the hold is issued once the court decides on the declaration.
Delinquent cases pick up a civil assessment (California caps it at $100) and move toward collections and licence action - Solano's own page is blunt about the sequence.
Traffic school needs a valid California licence, no school in the last 18 months and no mandatory appearance; the DMV's approved-school list is at selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/traffic/traffic-school.

Toll violations on the bridges and express lanes around Vallejo are not Superior Court traffic cases - they are handled by the tolling agency (Bay Area Toll Authority / FasTrak) under their own notice and appeal process.
Vallejo parking citations are issued by the City of Vallejo and paid to the city, not the court.
Ability-to-pay relief, a payment plan or community service can be requested through MyCitations; the earlier you ask, the more options the clerk still has.
