local.h: Visalia details, verified against Tulare County Superior Court
bullets: Visalia tickets go to the Superior Court of California, County of Tulare, with the traffic division reachable at (559) 730-5000 and (559) 782-3700, and payment possible online at the county's citation payment page or at any of its clerk's offices.
When you call or visit, Tulare asks you to have your citation number and your Reminder Notice in front of you - the clerk's office will not hunt the case for you.

You can go to arraignment without paying anything. The county says no bail or fee is required for arraignment and a later court trial unless, at arraignment, you refuse to sign a promise to appear for trial. At arraignment your rights and options are explained and you enter a plea.
You can also skip the separate arraignment and ask the clerk to set the arraignment and the court trial for the same time - most people who do that are avoiding two trips to the courthouse.

Trial by written declaration (Vehicle Code 40902) lets you resolve most cases without appearing at all: submit your declaration plus the bail forfeiture amount before the due date, in person or by mail. If you are found not guilty the money is refunded; if you are found guilty it is applied to the fine, with any difference refunded.
Financial hardship has three doors in Tulare: appear in person by appointment, mail a written request or form TR-320, or use the online ability-to-pay tool on MyCitations.

The officer who wrote the ticket is subpoenaed for a court trial, so a trial is not a formality - but neither is a conviction: if you are found guilty the judge sets the fine, which may be less than the bail deposit.
Failing to pay on time or respond to the citation adds penalties; the county warns about it on the same page that explains your options.
City of Visalia parking citations are handled by the city, not the court.

local.h: Concord details, verified against Contra Costa County Superior Court
bullets: Concord citations are filed with the Superior Court of California, County of Contra Costa. Traffic is administered county-wide, and the trial calendar for the Walnut Creek area sits in Department 50 (Walnut Creek and Richmond), with trials at 8:30 a.m. and arraignments at 9:30 a.m.
Pay through the county's payment portal or at the clerk's office between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. The court's traffic page is cc-courts.org/divisions/traffic.

The court does not handle parking tickets. Contra Costa states it plainly and tells drivers to contact the city printed on the ticket instead - which is why a Concord parking ticket and a Concord traffic ticket take different routes.

Miss the date on the reminder notice and the county adds a civil assessment of up to $100 and refers the case to its collection agency, Linebarger. The notice that tells you a civil assessment was added is simply telling you that the due date passed without payment.
Cannot afford the fine? The county uses form TR-320, Can't Afford to Pay Fine, and the court's hardship page explains the reduction, payment plan and community-service options.
Appearing remotely is possible: parties who want to appear for a hearing or arraignment should complete form TR-128 and file it in person or by mail at the courthouse named on the form.

Traffic school requests are handled by the court's traffic division; California's 18-month limit, the valid-licence requirement and the no-mandatory-appearance rule apply, with the DMV's approved list at selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/traffic/traffic-school.

Contra Costa has a beta assistant on its site, but the traffic page and the clerk's office are the reliable sources - and the county's own page is the one to quote if a third party tells you otherwise.

local.h: Chico details, verified against Butte County Superior Court
bullets: Chico's tickets are filed with the Superior Court of California, County of Butte, whose Traffic Division is at 1775 Concord Avenue, Chico, (530) 532-7005 - that is also where you go to set up a payment plan.

Pay online through the county's traffic payment page, by mail (check or money order in US dollars, payable to Butte County Superior Court, sent to the courthouse on your courtesy notice, with the case number and the name of the person cited written on it), or in person.

Payment plans have a down payment. Butte County requires 10% of the total bail at the time a bail instalment plan is set up, under Vehicle Code 40510.5 - a detail that surprises people who expect to start paying next month.

Do not use the online tool if you want to contest the citation, attend traffic school, or get a dismissal or reduction with proof of correction. Butte lists those three cases explicitly, and using the wrong route closes the case on the court's terms rather than yours.

Financial hardship: form Can't Afford to Pay Fine gets you a reduction, more time, a payment plan, or a work program converting the fine to community service - and Butte requires a financial declaration with income and expense evidence in most cases.
Butte County's traffic team also answers by phone at (530) 532-7014, which is the faster route for a question about a specific case number.
The county points hardship cases at MyCitations for pleading and requesting relief online on eligible infractions; misdemeanor and felony fines are not eligible.
City of Chico parking and downtown enforcement are city matters, not court cases.

local.h: Redding details, verified against Shasta County Superior Court

Pay online through the court's Pay Traffic Fines page, or in person at the courthouse in Redding. Bring the citation or case number - the clerk cannot search by name alone.

The county's traffic page links directly to MyCitations for ability-to-pay requests, which cover a reduced fine, a payment plan, more time to pay, or community service in lieu of fines on eligible infractions.

Traffic school: valid California licence, no school in the last 18 months, no mandatory-appearance violation; the approved provider list is maintained by the DMV, not the court, at selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/traffic/traffic-school.
Shasta County is where I-5 and Highway 44 enforcement happens, and CHP citations are filed with the same court as local ones - the issuing agency does not change your courthouse or deadline.
Contesting a citation here means a court trial or a trial by written declaration; ask the clerk which your violation allows before the due date, because filing a declaration requires posting bail.
Missing the due date leads to penalties, a possible licence hold and a collections referral; the court's remote-appearance page explains how to join a hearing if you are not local to Redding.
City of Redding parking citations are city cases - the court will not take them.

local.h: Merced details, verified against Merced County Superior Court

Walk-in arraignments are limited to Monday to Thursday mornings from 7:30 a.m. at the Merced traffic division - so a Friday walk-in will not resolve an arraignment.
Merced lists its traffic contacts by topic (case information, payments, traffic school), which is the fastest way to reach the right person before you drive downtown.

Financial hardship runs through MyCitations: a reduced fine, a payment plan, more time, or community service on eligible infractions. Do not use the tool if you want to contest, attend traffic school, or claim a proof-of-correction dismissal, and it is not for misdemeanors or felonies.
Juvenile traffic in Merced requires the minor to appear with a parent or guardian when the notice says the appearance is mandatory.

local.h: San Rafael details, verified against Marin County Superior Court
bullets: San Rafael is the seat of the Superior Court of California, County of Marin, and the county's traffic detail is unusually concrete on its payment options page - including which payment method releases a DMV hold fastest.

Cash is accepted only in person, in Room 113, from 8:00 a.m. Cheques, cashier's cheques and money orders payable to Marin County Superior Court can be mailed or paid in person in Room 113, and credit-card payments can be made in person, by mail with the stub from your Courtesy Notice, or by phone at (415) 448-8230 during business hours.

The licence-hold detail is the useful part: paying by personal cheque delays the DMV release of a hold on your licence or registration by ten calendar days. To have it released within 24 hours, pay by cash, cashier's cheque, money order or credit/debit card. If you are on a deadline with the DMV or your employer, that choice matters.
Credit-card payment with an international postal code will not go through the automated line - the court asks those callers to speak to a live operator during business hours.

Traffic school in Marin is requested with the full bail plus a $52 traffic school fee, so the payment you send has to cover both or the request is incomplete. The automated payment and enquiry line runs 24/7.
Write your case number or your name on the cheque or money order, and use the court's envelope - the county asks for both so the payment lands on the right case.
Proof of completion of community-service hours must be signed by the non-profit that supervised them if you are converting a fine to service hours.

Marin's mailing address for traffic is the court's Traffic P.O. Box - use the envelope in your Courtesy Notice rather than inventing an address, and note that San Rafael city parking citations are the city's business, not the court's.

local.h: Woodland details, verified against Yolo County Superior Court

The court's online payment system accepts Visa, MasterCard, American Express, Discover, Apple Pay and PayPal - a wider set than most California courts - and telephone payments go through the court's own line at (530) 406-6924 for Visa, MasterCard, American Express or Discover.

The walk-in payment centre takes cash, cheques, money orders, cashier's cheques and credit cards, and mail payments go to the Court Collections Division (write the case or account number on the payment).
Have your case number or account number ready for phone or online payments - the county asks for both up front, and credit-card details are taken on that line only during business hours.

Yolo County includes Davis, West Sacramento and Winters, so a citation written on I-80 or Highway 113 is still filed in Woodland - the courthouse on the ticket is the one that matters, not the city on the ticket.
Traffic school: California's once-every-18-months rule, valid licence and no mandatory appearance; the DMV's approved list is at selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/traffic/traffic-school.
Financial hardship, payment plans and community service are requested through the court or MyCitations - the court's payments page is the first stop for the paperwork.

local.h: Amarillo details, verified against Amarillo Municipal Court
bullets: Amarillo tickets are filed with the Amarillo Municipal Court, which takes payments and questions on (806) 378-3082. Its online system is the Municipal Online Services portal.
Warrants can be paid online here too. Amarillo's portal explicitly accepts most warrant payments, which is unusual - most Texas courts make you appear in person to clear a warrant.

The portal is also how you pay alternative sentencing amounts, including an approved Driving Safety Course or Deferred Disposition - but only once the court has granted it. Do not use the payment site to request a dismissal (for example a 'no driver's licence' charge that you can clear with proof).

Read this before you pay: the court states that paying through the service is a guilty plea and a waiver of a jury trial. If you want the DSC dismissal or a deferred disposition, request it first - paying closes the door on both.

Young drivers: Amarillo warns that if you were 24 or younger when you were cited, a Driving Safety Course may be required rather than optional, so check the court's instructions before treating a payment as the end of the matter.
Texas has no points system, but a conviction shows on your driving record and is visible to insurers - the reason a $10 DSC fee plus court costs is worth it on an eligible moving violation.

DSC eligibility and the state-approved course list are handled by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation: TDLR driving safety course search. You must request the course by your answer date and finish it within the time the court allows.
Citations written outside Amarillo city limits by a sheriff's deputy or state trooper go to the county Justice of the Peace, not the municipal court - check who issued the ticket.

local.h: Lubbock details, verified against Lubbock Municipal Court
bullets: Lubbock tickets are filed with the Lubbock Municipal Court, which handles payments and case questions on 806-775-2473. Its online portal is Municipal Online Services, and the court counter opens at 8:30 a.m.

Options show up only if they apply to your case. Lubbock's portal states that the Deferred Disposition and Driving Safety Course choices appear only when they are applicable to the citation you look up - so if you cannot see them, that is the system telling you the charge does not qualify (or the deadline has passed), not a bug.

Texas driving safety course, in plain terms: request it by your answer date, pay the court costs plus the state fee, then complete the course and file the certificate. Usually available once every 12 months, and not with a commercial licence.

A deferred disposition is the other Lubbock option on many moving violations: you plead no contest or guilty, pay a special expense fee, stay out of trouble for the deferral period, and the case is dismissed - typically for a shorter period than a conviction would stay on your insurance.

The approved course list is run by the state, not the city: any provider in the TDLR driving safety course search is what the court accepts. Do not buy a course from an out-of-state site that is not on that list.

Lubbock is in the South Plains, where a ticket can also be a county Justice of the Peace case (DPS or sheriff's deputy citations outside city limits) - the court name on your citation is what decides where you pay.
Missing an answer date in Texas is not a small matter: a failure to appear can bring a warrant and an additional fee, plus a possible licence or registration block.
Free expression of the fine does not matter online - the portal applies the court's schedule, and the amount it shows for your citation is the number to plan around.

local.h: McKinney details, verified against McKinney Municipal Court
bullets: McKinney citations go to the McKinney Municipal Court, reachable at 972-547-7676. Counter hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, and 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on Thursday - the Thursday start is an hour later than the rest of the week.
The court's online system is Municipal Online Services, and it lists its own services explicitly: plead and pay, pay a warrant, pay an approved payment plan, or pay a granted driving safety course.

What happens when you plead and pay online (the court says this in its own terms): you waive your right to a jury trial, waive discovery under the Code of Criminal Procedure, and a judgment of conviction is entered that may be reported to the Texas Department of Public Safety. If a reduced or dismissed outcome matters to you, do not lead with a payment.

If a driving safety course was already granted and you use the website to pay the remaining balance, the court treats that payment as a waiver of the show-cause hearing and a request for judgment - a real trap for people who meant to finish the course requirement.
Payments made after hours, at weekends or on a holiday do not post until the next business day. If your deadline lands on a holiday weekend, pay earlier rather than on the last evening.

Texas driving safety course basics: request it by your answer date, pay court costs plus the state fee, complete an approved course within the court's deadline. Providers are listed by the state at TDLR's driving safety course search.
Deferred disposition is the alternative on eligible moving violations - the court sets a deferral period and a special expense fee, and the charge is dismissed if you stay clean.
A citation issued by a Collin County deputy or a state trooper outside McKinney city limits belongs to a Justice of the Peace court, not the municipal court.

local.h: Grand Prairie details, verified against Grand Prairie Municipal Court
bullets: Grand Prairie tickets are filed with the Grand Prairie Municipal Court, which sits on the Dallas/Tarrant county line - so a citation may come from Grand Prairie police, a Dallas County constable, a Tarrant County deputy or the Department of Public Safety, and each goes to a different court.
The city's court payments run through Municipal Online Services, where you can look the case up by citation or driver's licence number.

The plea question is the important one. bullets: Civil traffic infractions in Florida are not filed in a courtroom. They are handled by the Clerk of the Circuit Court for the county where you were cited, and the clerk's office is where the money and the paperwork go - Leon County Clerk of Court and Comptroller.

You have 30 days to choose, and the three choices are: pay (that is an adjudication of guilt, with points on your Florida record), elect Basic Driver Improvement school (a 4-hour course; adjudication is withheld and no points are assessed), or request a hearing before a Traffic Hearing Officer to contest it. Doing nothing is not one of them.

Basic Driver Improvement is the Florida record-saver, but it has limits: you may elect it once in any 12-month period, it is not available to commercial driver's licence holders, and certain offences are excluded. The state's list of approved schools is at FLHSMV driver improvement schools.

Florida's point thresholds are statutory, not discretionary: 12 points in 12 months is a 30-day suspension, 18 in 18 months is three months, and 24 in 36 months is 12 months. You can see your own record through FLHSMV's driver licence check.

If you pay late you owe a late fee as well as the fine; a long enough non-payment can suspend your Florida licence and send the debt to the state's collection process, which adds a collection fee. Paying or electing school is always cheaper than ignoring the citation.

Many Florida counties can be paid through the state's county portal, MyFloridaCounty.com, which is a legitimate payment route operated for the clerks - and it is safer than any site that is not run by the clerk or the state.

New York's thresholds bite early: 6 points in 18 months triggers a Driver Responsibility Assessment of $100 a year for three years plus $25 for each point above 6, and 11 points in 18 months can suspend your licence. Points from a conviction stay on the record, typically for 18 months of counting.

Reducing the charge is how New York drivers really protect themselves: a plea to a non-moving violation (a parking or equipment infraction) carries no points at all, and that negotiation happens with the prosecutor or the court on the return date - not by paying the ticket as issued.

local.h: Hialeah details, verified against the Miami-Dade Clerk
bullets: Hialeah citations are Miami-Dade County cases, and the Clerk's own traffic page is where you work out which type you have: a civil traffic infraction (moving or non-moving, not punishable by jail, no jury trial and no right to appointed counsel) or a criminal traffic violation, which is a misdemeanour and where an arrest is possible.

That distinction decides everything. A civil infraction can be paid, deferred to school or contested on paper; a criminal traffic violation is a criminal case with a criminal calendar and should not be handled at a payment window.

Florida lets you elect a 4-hour Basic Driver Improvement course to keep the points off your record: adjudication is withheld and no points are assessed. You generally have 30 days from the citation, once in a 12-month period, and the election is made with the Clerk, not the police department.

Miami-Dade also handles parking citations separately - those are written to a vehicle for a county ordinance or state statute violation, and they are paid through the Clerk's parking route, not the moving-violation process. Hialeah writes a lot of both.
Florida assesses 3, 4 or 6 points per moving violation and suspends at 12 in 12 months, 18 in 18 or 24 in 36; points remain for three years.

local.h: Canton details, verified against the municipal court that covers the city
bullets: Ohio traffic tickets are municipal court cases. The court that covers Canton is the municipal court for that city - Ohio's municipal courts are city-based, not county-based, which is why the same county can have several of them and why the citation's court name matters.

Start from the city's own site: City of Canton points at that court's case search and payment options. Ohio courts show you the case record first - the online payment button only appears when the case is marked payable.
Canton Municipal Court is Stark County's biggest municipal court and runs its own case search, so you can look the case up and see whether it is marked payable before you pay anything.

Ohio assesses points on conviction, and 12 points in two years triggers a 12-point (class-D) suspension that typically runs six months. Points stay on the record for two years from the conviction, and the BMV can act before you reach twelve.

Ohio's record tool is not a dismissal - it is a 2-point credit. Completing a BMV-approved remedial driving course earns a credit against your point total; it does not delete the ticket unless a court orders it. Ask the court and check the BMV first, because paying for a course that does not change your case is a waste: Ohio BMV suspensions and remedial courses.

If the fine is the problem, Ohio courts can order a payment plan or community service instead of a single payment - that has to be asked for at the court, and it is much easier before the case is in default than after.
Check your point total at Ohio BMV. A conviction also reaches your insurer independently of the points.

local.h: Chandler details, verified against the court that covers the city
bullets: Most Arizona tickets are civil traffic violations, and they go to the city or justice court named on the citation. Criminal traffic charges - DUI, reckless driving, racing - go to the same court on a criminal docket, and those are not payable, they are appearances.

Chandler is in Maricopa County, where the Justice Courts handle most civil traffic cases countywide while each city also runs its own municipal court - Chandler has both a city court and access to the county justice court system.

Start with the court's own search: Maricopa County Justice Courts case lookup. Arizona courts publish a financial obligation figure for the case, which is the number with the state surcharges already added - the ticket amount is not it.

Arizona's serious route is the defensive driving dismissal. Complete a class at an Arizona Supreme Court certified school and the school notifies the court, so an eligible civil traffic violation is dismissed from your record - not just masked. Most drivers can use it once every 24 months, and CDL holders generally cannot.

Points are what make the dismissal worth it. Arizona tracks points on your MVD record, and accumulation leads to a suspension and a mandatory class. Because the points come from the conviction, a dismissal is a genuinely different outcome from paying the fine.

Arizona also expects a response from you by the date on the citation. Doing nothing is its own outcome: a failure to appear on a civil traffic case can end with your licence suspended, which is far more expensive than the fine.
Certified schools and program rules: Arizona Supreme Court - defensive driving program. Check your record at Arizona MVD.
